correctness.rationale: The lattice automorphisms are factorwise increasing maps and coordinate permutations (Kurilić 2026, Theorem 1.1(a)); labelled configurations are exactly tuples of weak orders with discrete meet of tie kernels. Inclusion–exclusion via partition-lattice Möbius removes non-distinct configurations, and an S_n×S_r fixed point decomposes into axis cycles whose allowable preorders descend exactly to b(g,P,length) equivalence blocks. A separate exhaustive orbit generator reproduces values for n<=3 and r<=4; the formula is proved for all stated finite n,r without relying on checks.

originality.rationale: The motivating current 2026 product-of-chains paper gives lattice factor rigidity without orbit numbers. The complete two-factor orbit sequence is explicitly covered by Cameron–Prellberg–Stark 2006 and not claimed as new. The 2025 multidimensional-permutation paper restricts to coordinate-injective patterns, whereas this formula handles ties and unordered coordinate factors for every r>=3. Targeted published-finding corpus and primary literature searches found no equal or stronger inspected statement; an inaccessible relevant report and alternate nomenclature remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-dimension expression solves a natural full finite-set-orbit profile of an omega-categorical distributive lattice class, not an arbitrary finite slice. It handles collisions and coordinate permutations simultaneously, yields the first five exact 3-factor counts, and extends the classical solved 2-factor incidence matrix census into every higher dimension. This invariant is needed to count isomorphism types of induced finite point arrangements and study finite-set orbit growth.
